components.text: Explain why potentially endless suffering is proportionate to finite wrongdoing and why rejection is culpable rather than confused.
Show that calling suffering internal rather than external answers the moral proportionality problem.
Whether resistance to painful sanctification can morally justify hell continuing without limit.
Whether a rejection of a perfectly loving God is genuinely culpable rather than the product of confusion.
Answer the charge that potentially infinite punishment is disproportionate to finite wrongdoing.
Answer the claim that rejection of perfect love is honest confusion rather than culpable choice.
Whether hell imposes an infinite punishment for finite wrongdoing.
Whether apparent rejection of perfect love reflects honest confusion rather than culpable persistence.
Explain how rejection can be culpable when apparent rejection of perfect love may instead reflect honest confusion.
Whether rejection of God must be confusion rather than a morally attributable choice.
Show why subconscious emotional or identity bias supplies control over the resulting belief.
Whether subconscious bias and emotional motivation establish morally relevant control over belief.
Explain how a person can exercise control despite subconscious influences on belief.
Whether subconscious influences remain beyond meaningful reflective control.
Show why identity-driven or irrational belief is a morally punishable choice rather than psychologically caused conviction.
Distinguish motivational influence from voluntary selection of belief.
Whether identity-driven irrational belief is a meaningful choice fit for moral punishment.
Whether psychological motivation turns the resulting conviction into culpable belief.
Explain why an omnipotent loving God may permit harmful rejection produced through obscure or misleading information channels.
Show that self-correction remains a sufficient answer when the divine source does not make itself adequately known.
Whether promising mercy for honest error adequately answers preventable divine misinformation.
Whether rejection remains culpable when God communicates through ambiguous intermediaries.
Explain why perfect love permits preventable misinformation to produce harmful self-exile.
Explain why increasingly harmful character remains attributable rather than psychologically determined.
Whether a loving omnipotent God must correct preventable misinformation before permitting self-exile.
Whether psychologically determined belief is an improper basis for moral punishment.
Explain whether internal degeneration morally justifies an everlasting state from which escape is impossible.
Assess the defended annihilationist and honest-error qualifications rather than only a different popular doctrine.
Whether the defended annihilationist and mercy-qualified account is itself morally coherent.
Whether internal degeneration remains morally objectionable under the defended qualified account.
Answer whether the defended account makes hell everlasting and impossible to escape.
Explain how the account avoids an infinite consequence for finite wrongdoing.
Whether hell must be everlasting and inescapable once a soul enters it.
Whether potentially endless punishment is avoided by eventual annihilation.
Explain how remaining in hell can be an informed autonomous choice if any willing soul may leave.
Distinguish culpable resistance from inability to endure painful rehabilitation.
Whether formal permission to turn back makes continued hell an informed autonomous choice.
Whether painful attachment to sin explains continued separation without incapacity or mistake.
Explain how a soul that wants escape but lacks strength can actually leave hell.
Explain what happens when sanctification remains painful after the soul seeks rescue.
Whether a soul wanting escape may nevertheless lack the strength or ability to leave hell.
Whether painful sanctification prevents rescue even after a soul seeks help.
Explain who can permanently remain in hell if seekers receive grace and genuinely mistaken souls receive mercy.
Reconcile forgiveness of honest misinformation with the existence of permanently separated souls.
Whether limiting rescue to willing seekers leaves any morally permissible soul permanently in hell.
Whether mercy for genuinely mistaken souls covers everyone who does not seek rescue.
Explain why Christ's rescue mechanism is grounded if he does not undergo humanity's consequence of death or separation.
Whether grace has an adequate theological basis for carrying willing souls out of hell.
Whether death or annihilation is the consequence that Christ must bear on humanity's behalf.
Show that Christ undergoes the death and separation identified as humanity's consequences for sin.
Whether Christ undergoes the death and separation identified as humanity's consequences for sin.
Explain why a temporary crucifixion and subsequent exaltation adequately match humanity's allegedly grave consequence.
Whether temporary crucifixion and subsequent exaltation adequately match the alleged consequence and moral weight of sin.
Explain why Christ's bounded crucifixion can nonetheless constitute a proportionately immense sacrifice.
Whether Christ's temporary suffering is sufficiently costly to answer for the world's sins.
